title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Scammers have deployed AI systems to create deepfakes and clone voices for impersonation fraud targeting immigrants and families in Georgia and South Florida. The systems generated fake identities of real professionals, including an immigration attorney, to solicit money from victims seeking legal services or responding to emergency requests. This is impersonation at scale: voice cloning and synthetic media made the fraudulent interactions convincing enough to extract hundreds of thousands of dollars before detection.

The failure occurred in the deployment phase, where no verification gate stood between the impersonated identity and the victim's decision to send money. The systems were not built to defraud anyone, but placed in service of fraud by criminals who obtained source material from social media. What would have caught this: victims verifying requests through independently known contact information, and platforms limiting access to voice cloning tools or flagging their use.

It is not established whether the AI tools were purpose-built for fraud or diverted from legitimate uses by the criminals who deployed them.

summary:
Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence to create deepfakes and clone voices to commit fraud across Georgia and South Florida. A South Florida immigration attorney discovered criminals had cloned his voice and identity to target immigrants seeking legal help, while a Cobb County couple lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in AI-enabled scam losses last year, with Florida reporting 350 AI-related complaints totaling $39.9 million and Georgia reporting 71 complaints totaling $10.4 million in losses.

Criminals are using generative AI to make traditional scams more convincing by cloning voices from social media, spoofing phone numbers, creating fake photographs, and researching victims' family relationships. The AI grandparent scam involves criminals using voice cloning to impersonate grandchildren claiming to need urgent money. Financial institutions warn that AI makes impersonation increasingly difficult to detect. Experts recommend families establish code words to verify identity during emergencies, verify urgent requests through known phone numbers, and avoid sending money based solely on phone calls.
